title: Lesson 089 · The Processor City: Architecture Overview
intro: Catch up on the key A Level ideas. Complete four retrieval questions, work through the examples, then practise and explain your reasoning.

questions.prompt: Choose the model answer: What is the function of a program counter?
Choose the model answer: What does the ALU perform?
Choose the model answer: Name one type of bus.
Choose the model answer: A D flip-flop has D=1 and Q=0 just before the active rising edge. What is Q after the edge?
questions.answer: Q becomes1, as D is sampled at the active edge.
options: Q becomes1, as D is sampled at the active edge.
questions.feedback: Q becomes1, as D is sampled at the active edge.

blocks.title: Observe
blocks.text: Inside CPU City Hall, the Control Unit organises operations, the ALU carries out arithmetic and logic, and registers hold immediate working state.

blocks.title: Explain
blocks.text: The Memory Warehouse stores program instructions and data. Address, data and control buses connect processor and memory; they carry different kinds of information.

blocks.title: Evaluate
blocks.text: Von Neumann architecture stores instructions and data in a shared memory/address space, whereas Harvard uses separate instruction and data memories/pathways.

blocks.title: Worked example · Model response
blocks.text: The address identifies where; data is what is transferred. CU coordinates the process.
